title: Complete algebra devissages on finitely many etale charts covering a fibre
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Use chartwise local finite type and local finite presentation [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact, with quasi-compact diagonal. A module of finite type is locally finitely generated on etale scheme charts; a finitely presented module has locally an exact presentation $\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^s\to M\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Let $f:X\to Y$ be of finite presentation with $Y$ a scheme, let $M$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent module on $X$, and let $y\in Y$. There exist an affine etale neighbourhood $(Y\prime,y\prime)\to(Y,y)$ and finitely many affine schemes $W_j$, representable etale maps $h_j:W_j\to X_{Y\prime}$, such that each $W_j\to Y\prime$ is of finite presentation, and the union of the images $h_j(W_j)$ contains the entire fibre $|(X_{Y\prime})_{y\prime}|$. Write $Y\prime=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $W_j=\operatorname{Spec}A_j$ and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ for $y\prime$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. If $M_j=h_j^*M_{Y\prime}$ and $N_j=\Gamma(W_j,M_j)$, then $N_j/A_j/R$ has a complete algebra devissage over $\mathfrak p$ [def-trf-complete-algebra-devissage]. The empty family is allowed for an empty fibre.

source.place: Tag 0CWJ (spaces-flat-lemma-existence-complete), specialized to finite presentation; affine algebra formulation Tag 05HX (definition-complete-devissage-algebra), corresponding to Tags 05H4 and 05HH.

proof.text: Open immersions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Choose an affine open neighbourhood $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $y$ and put $X_0=X\times_Y Y_0$. Quasi-compactness of $f$ gives quasi-compactness of $X_0$ by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. The atlas characterization there, together with the last clause of [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas], also gives quasi-compactness of its point space. Apply [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] to obtain an affine scheme $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and a representable surjective etale map $V\to X_0$. All maps $V\to X$ in this construction are etale by base change and composition [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. The chart test in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] makes $V\to Y_0$ locally of finite presentation. Thus $A$ is finitely presented over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation].

source.place: Tag 0CWJ (lemma-existence-complete), proof: reduce to affine base and an affine surjective etale atlas; finite-presentation specialization.

proof.text: Let $F$ be the restriction of $M$ to $V$. It is the tensor pullback in the question: the etale restriction comparison of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization] identifies them. The affine chart theorem [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] gives a finite $A$-module $N=F(V)$ and identifies $F$ with its associated module sheaf; in fact $N$ is finitely presented. Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ correspond to $y$. For every $v\in V_y$, corresponding to $\mathfrak q\subset A$ over $\mathfrak p$, apply [lem-trf-complete-algebra-devissage-etale-existence] to $R\to A,N,\mathfrak q$. Write its output as $R_v,A_v,\mathfrak p_v,\mathfrak q_v$ and $U_v=\operatorname{Spec}A_v$, $T_v=\operatorname{Spec}R_v$. It supplies etale maps $U_v\to V$, $T_v\to Y_0$, residue-field isomorphisms at both chosen primes, and a complete algebra devissage of $(N\otimes_A A_v)/A_v/R_v$ over $\mathfrak p_v$.

source.place: Tag 0CWJ and Tags 05HU (lemma-existence-complete), 05I1 (lemma-existence-algebra): choose pointwise algebra devissages on the atlas.

proof.text: The map $U_v\to V_{T_v}$ is etale: both $U_v$ and $V_{T_v}$ are etale over $V$, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], so apply cancellation in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Pull it back to the chosen point $\mathfrak p_v$ of $T_v$. Since $\kappa(\mathfrak p_v)=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, this gives an etale map $(U_v)_{\mathfrak p_v}\to V_y$ whose image $O_v$ is open by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover] (applied to scheme targets), and contains $v$ because of $\mathfrak q_v$. The affine fibre formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $V_y$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$, hence it is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Select finitely many $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ for which the opens $O_{v_i}$ cover $V_y$. Here the finite-subcover assertion is exactly the definition of quasi-compactness. If $V_y$ is empty, take $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 05HU, proof: finite subcover by the images on the chosen residue-field fibre. The elementary residue-field identifications ensure this is a cover of the whole fibre, not just selected points.

proof.text: Abbreviate the chosen data by $R_i,A_i,\mathfrak p_i,U_i,T_i$. Put $T=T_1\times_{Y_0}\cdots\times_{Y_0}T_n=\operatorname{Spec}C$, with $C=R_1\otimes_R\cdots\otimes_R R_n$, and take $T=Y_0$ for $n=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. By etale base change and composition [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], $T\to Y_0\to Y$ is etale. The chosen maps $R_i\to\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ agree on $R$, and their product on pure tensors defines $C\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Its kernel $\mathfrak r$ is prime and contracts to $\mathfrak p_i$ in every $R_i$. Its residue field is $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$: the image subring contains $R/\mathfrak p$ inside its fraction field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, so its fraction field is that same field. Let $t\in T$ denote this point. Thus $(T,t)\to(Y,y)$ is the required common affine etale neighbourhood.

source.place: Tag 05HU, proof: finite fibre product of elementary etale base neighbourhoods and its distinguished residue-field point.

proof.text: Set $W_i=U_i\times_{T_i}T=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i\otimes_{R_i}C)$ [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Each $W_i\to V_T$ is the base change of $U_i\to V_{T_i}$, hence etale; composing with the etale atlas $V_T\to X_T$ gives a representable etale map $h_i:W_i\to X_T$ [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. On fibres at $t$ these maps to $V_t=V_y$ are the maps $(U_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}\to V_y$, since all distinguished base residue fields are $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Equivalently their images are the pullbacks of $O_{v_i}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image]. They cover $V_t$ by Step 3. The atlas is still surjective on the fibre by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], so their images in $X_t$ cover all of $|X_t|$. For $n=0$, surjectivity of the atlas implies $X_t$ is empty.

source.place: Tags 0CWJ and 05HU: base change the chosen charts and check that their images still cover the entire fibre.

proof.text: It remains to check finite presentation of $W_i\to T$. By [def-weil-etale-morphism], the affine etale map $U_i\to V_{T_i}$ is locally of finite presentation, hence its coordinate algebra map $A\otimes_R R_i\to A_i$ is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]. The algebra $A\otimes_R R_i$ is finitely presented over $R_i$: tensor a fixed finite polynomial presentation of $A/R$ with $R_i$ to obtain exactly the same generators and relations with coefficients mapped to $R_i$. Composing the two locally finitely presented scheme maps is locally finitely presented by [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition], so $A_i/R_i$ has a finite polynomial presentation by the same affine criterion. Tensor that presentation with $C$; it presents $A_i\otimes_{R_i}C$ by finitely many generators and relations over $C$. Thus $W_i\to T$ is locally of finite presentation, and it is affine: the affine target $T$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated] applied to its structure map, so [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-separated-target-affine-morphism] applies to $W_i\to T$. Therefore it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. This is finite presentation with precisely the convention in the question.

source.place: Tag 0CWJ, finite-presentation specialization; Morphisms Tag 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize), composition and the explicit base change of polynomial presentations.

proof.text: Write $N_i=N\otimes_A A_i$. On $U_i$ this is the sections module of the restriction of $M$, and on $W_i$ its sections are $N_i\otimes_{R_i}C$. These are affine scheme maps: use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated] for the affine target and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-separated-target-affine-morphism] for the map. Indeed [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies the etale and Zariski tensor pullbacks; the affine-section formula of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change] applied to $U_i\to T_i$ gives exactly this tensor module. The composition comparison of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization] identifies it with $\Gamma(W_i,h_i^*M_T)$, with the pullback convention of the item. By Step 2, $N_i/A_i/R_i$ has a complete algebra devissage over $\mathfrak p_i$. Apply [lem-sfb-complete-algebra-devissage-base-change] to $R_i\to C$ and the prime $\mathfrak r$ contracting to $\mathfrak p_i$. It gives a complete algebra devissage of $(N_i\otimes_{R_i}C)/(A_i\otimes_{R_i}C)/C$ over $\mathfrak r$, as required. Finally take $(Y\prime,y\prime)=(T,t)$ and rename the finitely many charts. No flatness of $M$ was used.
